title: SLO-aware trippoint synthesizer + regional fallback heuristics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Design and implement a unified SLO-aware "trippoint synthesizer" that computes safe circuit-breaker trip thresholds at dependency/model/tenant granularity, and a deterministic set of regional fallback heuristics that select safe fallbacks while minimizing user-visible regression.

Background: Current breakers are configured with static thresholds or naive spike guards. We need an approach that respects per-tenant SLOs (latency/availability/quality), per-model resource characteristics, and regional capacity constraints. The synthesizer should be able to emit: (1) soft trip (degrade preference), (2) hard trip (reject/redirect), and (3) probation windows for automatic recovery.

Key design ideas:
- Input signals: 1s/10s/1m latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), recent error rate, CPU/GPU util, queue length, cold-start rate, per-tenant SLOs (from tenant metadata), model quality drift signals (eval delta), and regional capacity headroom.
- Scoring: compute a normalized risk score per (tenant, model, region) by combining weighted z-scores from latency/error/util; apply tenant SLO weight to bias toward stricter protection for high-SLA tenants. Use EWMA smoothing and an outlier dampener that uses a short-term percentile (e.g., p99 over 30s) to avoid noisy trips from single spikes.
- Threshold synthesis: convert risk score into trippoints using configurable hysteresis windows (grow/shrink windows) and a severity bucketing scheme (green/yellow/red). Green->no action, Yellow->soft-degrade (route to cached/cheaper variant, enable KV prefix caching), Red->hard-trip (route to fallback region/model or reject).
- Fallback selection heuristics: prioritized list based on: (a) compatibility (same model family/architecture), (b) expected quality delta (must be within tenant quality budget), (c) cost delta (prefer cheaper only when quality delta acceptable), (d) region affinity & data residency, (e) cold-start risk. Heuristics expose a tunable policy matrix per customer tier.
- Safe fallback orchestration: when opening a breaker, perform an immediate dark-launch of fallback path for 30s capturing golden/validation queries before routing traffic; if validation passes (fallback_quality_regression < configured budget), then gradually shift traffic along a linear or sigmoid schedule with traffic mirrors for quality comparison; maintain a penalty-box queue for overflow which accepts a limited, rate-limited fraction for retry.
- Multi-region failover specifics: prefer intra-region model variants for latency when headroom allows; in cross-region fallbacks, add region penalty to risk score and require stricter validation (higher probation). Implement region-level hysteresis to prevent flapping when multi-region sync delays occur.

Observability & telemetry to add:
- metrics: computed_trip_score, trip_state, trip_cause, trip_duration, fallback_selected, fallback_validation_pass, fallback_latency_delta, fallback_quality_regression, penalty_box_size, probation_success_rate.
- traces: attach decision context (inputs used, weights, last model eval delta) to sampled traces for postmortem.
- dashboards: per-tenant heatmap of trip activity, per-model break histories, regional failover latency/quality rollups.

Safety & rollout controls:
- feature-flagged at org and tenant granularity.
- dark launch: compute trippoints and log actions without action for 2 weeks; run an automated simulation harness to compare synthesized trips vs historical incidents.
- canary: enable modulation for 1% of traffic for three customers (small, mid, enterprise) for 72 hours; require <0.5% regression in end-to-end quality and <2% client-visible latency increase for promotion.
- rollback: automated rollback on any open incident exceeding X minutes or >1% error spike.

Testing & simulation:
- build a trace-replay simulator that replays 30, 90, 180 day windows of traffic and verifies trippoint stability, false-positive rate, and fallback success rate.
- run A/B experiments with golden queries to measure fallback accuracy.

Success criteria (initial):
- reduce tenant-level P95 unplanned outage time by 30% in months with trips,
- false positive trips < 3% of total trip events in simulation,
- fallback validation pass rate >= 98% in canary,
- no customer escalation caused by fallback in first 30 days of rollout.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Spec & simulation harness (2 weeks) -> Confluence design + replay harness prototype.
2) Producer for synthesized trippoints + telemetry (3 weeks) -> publish to routing/dispatcher service via protobuf.
3) Fallback selection service & validation mirror (2 weeks) -> light-weight validator using golden set.
4) Integration with runtime routing + penalty box (2 weeks) -> feature-flagged rollout.
5) Canary + ramp + full rollout (4 weeks)

Migration notes: existing static breakers remain authoritative until migration switch flips per tenant. Document expected behavioral diffs and provide an operator UI to view inferred trippoints and manual overrides.
